memory_update.text: FCPT should be retained as the cleanest underfollowed public proxy for restaurant net-lease real estate and sale-leaseback exposure; verify Darden concentration and other-restaurant rent coverage in Layer 2.
EPRT should be retained as a diversified sale-leaseback capital provider with restaurant/QSR exposure; exposure purity is lower than FCPT but middle-market franchisee relevance may be higher.

The restaurant expansion chokepoint may be less about brand demand and more about franchisee access to acceptable capital: bank loans, SBA credit, sale-leasebacks, rent coverage, and remodel financing.

No strong US-listed pure-play restaurant remodel contractor or site-selection/data provider was proven in this pass; future searches should test construction services, permitting, kitchen equipment finance, and location analytics vendors.

summary: Expanded the universe around the second-order capacity node where restaurant/franchise growth depends on real-estate capital, sale-leaseback availability, SBA/franchise credit, and unit-level rent coverage. The cleanest public-market mappings are restaurant-heavy net-lease REITs and specialty lenders. FCPT and EPRT are the strongest underfollowed candidates because their portfolios explicitly connect to restaurant/QSR tenants and sale-leaseback capital. AX is a niche public bank with explicit QSR franchise-finance marketing. RC is a below-$300M speculative exception because it directly markets SBA franchise lending but needs verification of revenue materiality and credit quality.
